authority: ComTool.Migration.Parity (parity manifest is lane-owned; matrix is the legacy oracle)

policy.parityIsNotCliShapeEquality: A legacy subcommand and a V2 operation are not required to share a name, argument grammar, or envelope layout. Parity is judged on the semantic capability the caller can still reach and on whether V2 states uncertainty truthfully.

states.implemented: The capability is reachable in V2 through registered production operations and has conformance test evidence.
states.partial: A meaningful subset of the capability is reachable; named aspects are listed in missingAspects.
states.superseded: The capability is reachable only through a different, deliberately stronger abstraction. Not a regression.
states.intentional_drop: The legacy capability is deliberately absent from V2 and must not be reintroduced.
states.missing: The matrix names a V2 operation that does not exist in the production operation catalog.

capabilityDispositions.retained: The legacy capability survives with comparable semantics.
capabilityDispositions.replaced_by_stronger_abstraction: The legacy abstraction is gone but a strictly safer V2 mechanism carries the intent.
capabilityDispositions.intentionally_not_retained: The legacy capability itself is rejected and has no V2 equivalent.

policy.catalogPresenceRule: Catalog presence is required only for v2Operations entries with production=true. Entries with kind facet|type|policy|transport name architecture, not a registered operation, and are never catalog-gated.
policy.evidenceRule: Every implemented mapping needs at least one evidence reference. kind=test evidence additionally requires the symbol to be present in the file, so a renamed or deleted test class fails the gate. Test counts are never asserted.

mappings.capability: Read host liveness, build/version identity, document count, and the active-document summary without conflating host health with script-engine health.
intentionalIncompatibilities: V2 splits runtime health from target status; the legacy conflation is rejected.

mappings.capability: Capture active-document and selection state as one bounded, machine-readable observation.
intentionalIncompatibilities: The matrix names the operation host.snapshot; the registered operation is core.target.snapshot. The facet ISnapshotProvider still provides it. Naming drift only, not a capability gap.

mappings.capability: Resolve a dotted COM path with 0-based collection indices and read one property.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Empty path segments are rejected instead of collapsing silently.
Nested object summaries are re-read through the retry policy instead of un-retried getattr chains.

mappings.capability: Write one direct COM property with declared mutation safety and postcondition support.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Generic com.set is a fixed external-side-effect escape hatch with a required lease; caller-supplied effects cannot downgrade it.

Known positive inventory signatures are enforced before target discovery/worker dispatch (including primitive and enum setter domains). Because the inventory source has no authoritative Illustrator version, unresolved members remain intentionally late-bound rather than becoming a false denylist.
Prefer the typed illustrator.* mutation operations when a first-class property domain exists.

mappings.capability: Invoke a COM method with JSON arguments, with mutation risk classified from the operation rather than the raw method name.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Generic com.call is a fixed external-side-effect escape hatch with a required lease; method mutation risk is never inferred from the raw method name.

Known inventory arity and concrete primitive/enum domains are enforced before target discovery/worker dispatch. Source VT_VARIANT parameters and unresolved/version-ambiguous signatures remain intentionally late-bound rather than being assigned guessed semantic domains.

Use typed operations for semantic domains the type library encodes only as VT_VARIANT; for example illustrator.document.close owns the explicit save/discard/prompt/reject-if-dirty policy instead of treating Document.Close(Boolean) as a typed contract.

mappings.capability: Run ExtendScript in the host with faithful argument and return types and non-replayable mutation semantics.
intentionalIncompatibilities: A result string that merely looks like JSON is never re-interpreted as JSON; type identity comes from the script codec.
Static ES3 preflight is advisory and never claimed as live-engine equivalence.

mappings.capability: Run a JSX file with Adobe preprocessor directives through the host's own directive-aware route.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Directive-bearing files are routed through the directive-aware host path instead of the inject-then-eval path, so arguments and return behavior no longer differ silently by route.

mappings.capability: Reject unsupported script syntax before spending a host call, without overclaiming live-engine equivalence.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Validation is explicitly advisory static analysis; only script.eval or script.runFile can provide live-engine truth.

mappings.capability: Run a named Illustrator action with bounded polling and an explicit postcondition.
intentionalIncompatibilities: V2 never mutates process-global UserInteractionLevel; the explicit DoScript dialog flag is the only dialog policy.
A run already busy before dispatch is refused instead of being attributed to the caller.

mappings.capability: Open a document with explicit lifecycle ownership instead of implicit active-document state.
intentionalIncompatibilities: The matrix names the operation document.open; the registered operation is illustrator.document.open. Naming drift only.

mappings.capability: Close a document under a save policy the caller cannot misread.
intentionalIncompatibilities: The Boolean save argument is dropped. Illustrator expects an AiSaveOptions domain value, and an implicit save/discard default is unsafe.
Replacement policy vocabulary is explicit: save, discard, prompt, reject_if_dirty.
The matrix names the operation document.close; the registered operation is illustrator.document.close. Naming drift only.

mappings.capability: Run several operations in one host session without continuing past a failed prerequisite.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Continue-after-failure is not the default: dependent workflows fail fast unless the step declares otherwise.
A workflow runs under a target lease; the legacy batch held only a process-local named mutex.
Submission is asynchronous with an explicit status handle; the legacy batch was a synchronous in-process loop.

mappings.capability: Persist steps across calls and resume, without blind replay of a mutation whose dispatch is unknown.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Persisted done entries are never blindly re-dispatched. A step whose mutation dispatch is uncertain becomes a durable mutation incident requiring explicit reconciliation.
The legacy at-least-once replay guarantee is deliberately not reproduced.
Multi-writer races are resolved by a revisioned durable store rather than file-level races.

mappings.capability: Keep one host session alive across many commands, with transport parity across stdio, pipe, and MCP.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Session continuity is owned by the runtime/supervisor pair, not by keeping one client process alive. A dropped client process does not lose an owned worker.
The legacy --stay help wording implied persistence across later processes; that claim is not reproduced.

mappings.capability: Poll a host condition until it is satisfied, with bounded timing and honest equality semantics.
intentionalIncompatibilities: V2 watch sources must be registered read-only operations; arbitrary script.eval cannot self-certify as a safe polling source.
Poll intervals are bounded away from zero so a watch cannot hammer Illustrator.

mappings.capability: Cross-process agent-owned arbitrary state with an operation counter.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Filename-sanitized session names alias distinct agents, so the abstraction is unsound as a concurrency primitive.
The file-backed counter is not host session state and loses updates under multi-writer access.
V2 exposes real runtime/debug/workflow continuity handles instead. Do not reintroduce a file-backed named session as a foundation.

mappings.capability: Own a spawned child process with a durable record that cannot cancel or finalize by PID reuse alone.
intentionalIncompatibilities: V2 does not persist a bare child PID and later kill it; workflow cancellation is a CAS-style durable job-state request and every host step re-enters the authoritative dispatcher.
Workflow ownership persists the runtime PID plus process start time; an orphaned running job becomes interrupted and requires explicit resume.
A parent workflow cannot report success while a failed child step is hidden.

mappings.capability: Attach to the Adobe ExtendScript debugger, keep a persistent conversation, and manage host-persisted breakpoints.
intentionalIncompatibilities: The debugger session is worker-owned and persistent, not one process per invocation. debug.session.status is read-only and needs no lease, because observing session ownership is not debugger use.
Session identity is invalidated on host restart rather than reused.

mappings.capability: REPL-style debugger control: evaluate in a suspended frame, step, continue, and read frames and properties.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Debugger interaction is stateful by design. A stateless CLI invocation that pretends a step is independent is rejected.
Bridge startup time is watchdog-bounded and owned by the session rather than blocking an unbounded client call.

mappings.capability: Serialize host automation with an identity-checked lease that survives process death without losing mutation truth.
intentionalIncompatibilities: The lock is per target, not one global COM mutex, so unrelated hosts do not serialize against each other.
Abandoned-lock recovery proves only deadlock recovery, never document consistency; a mutation that was in flight stays a durable incident.
The legacy metadata file was not ProgID-scoped and had release/delete races; V2 has no such file.

mappings.capability: Retry only known transient COM failures with bounded backoff, without overshooting the deadline or hiding execution certainty.
intentionalIncompatibilities: A generic server fault is classified for execution certainty rather than being retried blindly.
A local timeout is never treated as proof that the host operation did not execute.

mappings.capability: Discover and bind to a host process with strong identity and explicit ownership of a launched host.
intentionalIncompatibilities: V2 never implicitly launches while attaching: discovery, exact-generation attach, and launch are separate explicit operations.
Attaching to a preexisting generation never transfers ownership to the runtime.
A launch whose resulting generation cannot be proven remains unproven and does not authorize cleanup or silent retry.
Every target identity is bound to host family, PID, process start time, executable path, and endpoint identity through the strong target id.

mappings.capability: One machine-readable envelope per operation with orthogonal status, retryability, and execution certainty.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Retryability and execution certainty are separate fields instead of being inferred from a message string.
Nested failures cannot be reported as outer success.
Exit-code classes are a CLI transport concern; the protocol itself carries status rather than an exit code.

mappings.capability: Keep oversized results out of the caller's context using a size-measured, expiring, content-addressable reference.
intentionalIncompatibilities: V2 uses opaque runtime artifact IDs rather than exposing temporary filesystem paths.

The authenticated runtime-to-worker broker retains the public 1 MiB frame ceiling; large successful result payloads use correlated bounded chunk frames so only the sole runtime process commits the artifact store.

mappings.capability: Move script values between the host and the client without losing type identity, with acceleration that is never load-bearing for correctness.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Correctness semantics do not depend on a native acceleration lane; the hash-pinned ES3 ESON runtime is the production correctness surface.
Optional acceleration is permitted only when it preserves identical codec semantics and therefore is intentionally not an agent-visible capability toggle.
The codec is hash-pinned and namespaced so it cannot clobber unrelated shared JSON or ESPACK state in the host engine.

mappings.capability: Give an agent accurate, machine-readable examples and descriptions that cannot drift from the parser.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Human-oriented Markdown command reference is not the discovery authority; the runtime catalog and machine-readable example registry are.
Example target/lease/mutation metadata is derived from the live OperationDefinition instead of being authored independently.

mappings.capability: Search a versioned type-library inventory for interfaces, signatures, enums, and interface paths.
intentionalIncompatibilities: The runtime never opens the legacy SQLite or multi-megabyte JSON inventory at request time; it serves a deterministic SHA-verified embedded pack generated offline from the authoritative SQLite/manifest revision.
The build-machine Illustrator version is explicitly non-authoritative; the inventory host version remains unknown unless the source manifest itself declares one.

mappings.capability: Reach a native plug-in that exposes a compatible messaging contract, with durable truth about side effects.
intentionalIncompatibilities: An ambiguous plug-in message becomes a durable mutation incident requiring explicit reconciliation instead of a retryable error.
The bridge is explicitly not arbitrary native debugger access.

mappings.capability: Choose explicitly among direct COM, injected JSX, action, and native plug-in routes, without hidden heuristics.
intentionalIncompatibilities: V2 deliberately has no hidden fallback chain. The caller selects an explicit registered route after catalog and live-target capability discovery.
Undocumented menu strings are never silently substituted for a failed COM/script/action route.
Each route retains its own mutation class, lease, replay, watchdog, and reconciliation semantics.

mappings.capability: Cross-process durable records that survive concurrent writers without silently resetting on corruption.
intentionalIncompatibilities: The V2 store is private to the V2 runtime and is intentionally not a shared record format with the legacy tool. An agent must not hand-edit V2 state files.
Corrupt state is quarantined, not treated as missing and silently overwritten.

mappings.capability: Validate the highest-risk implementation surface, not just documentation assets.
intentionalIncompatibilities: Validation is a per-project unit, fake-host, live-host, and adapter test suite rather than one script that inspects Markdown.
The legacy validator did not validate the comtool implementation; that gap is not reproduced.
